notes: Architectural rule #1 (no direct service-to-service calls) is violated in the router: the router calls this.users.get() to validate users before comment/task/member operations, and calls this.projects.get() to validate projects before task creation, and calls this.tasks.get() to get assignee before enriching the comment.added.enriched event. This cross-service data access in the router is itself a rule #3 concern — rule #3 says 'all HTTP handling is in the API Router only,' which is satisfied, but the router is doing cross-service orchestration/validation that implicitly couples services. The 'comment.added.enriched' event emitted directly from the router (not from CommentService) is a workaround for not being able to access task assignee in NotificationService — this is a design smell and reveals a deeper architectural problem: NotificationService cannot properly handle comment.added without knowing the assignee, which the CommentService cannot provide without querying TaskService (violating rule #1). The workaround leaks business logic into the router. Rule #2 is mostly respected (each service has its own Map). Rule #4 (forward-only transitions) is correctly implemented. Rule #5 (no external npm deps) is respected; shims.d.ts is used for built-in modules, which is unusual and unnecessary since TypeScript has built-in types for node — the shims shadow proper typings and use 'any' extensively, reducing type safety. Rule #6 (each service in its own file) is satisfied. Completeness is good: all CRUD operations are implemented for all five services, status transitions work, assign/member endpoints exist, notifications for all three events exist (with the workaround), and a working demo script is present. The task spec uses 'assigneeId' but implementation uses 'assignee' inconsistently. Project spec uses 'memberIds' but implementation uses 'members'. The 204 response sends an empty JSON object body '{}' which is unconventional (204 should have no body). Error swallowing in EventBus is silent with no logging. The update endpoint for tasks allows overwriting projectId which could corrupt data integrity. Overall a functional implementation with notable architectural compromises.
